findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.assumptions: The 'size' parameter passed to 'dot_product' is not validated to be less than or equal to 'SIZE'. If an attacker can control the 'size' parameter, they could potentially cause a buffer overflow.

findings.title: Uninitialized Memory Access
findings.assumptions: The 'malloc' calls do not check if they return NULL, which would indicate that memory allocation failed. If memory allocation fails, dereferencing the pointers 'a' and 'b' will lead to undefined behavior.

findings.title: Format String Vulnerability
findings.assumptions: The 'result' variable, which is derived from the dot product calculation, is not controlled by the attacker. However, if there is any possibility of format string vulnerabilities due to other parts of the code, this should be considered.

findings.title: Resource Leak
findings.trigger: free is not called if an error occurs before reaching the free calls
findings.assumptions: The 'free' calls are only made if the program reaches the end of the 'main' function without encountering any errors. If an error occurs before reaching these calls, memory will be leaked.
